questions.question: Which of the following substituents, when present on a benzene ring, directs an incoming electrophile mainly to the meta position?
options: $-NHCOCH_3$
$-CHO$
$-Cl$

solution.key_concept: Groups with a pi bond to an electronegative atom on the atom attached to the ring withdraw electrons by -R/-I. They are meta directing.
steps: In $-CHO$, the carbon attached to the ring carries a $C=O$ pi bond, so the group withdraws electrons by -R/-I.
This makes the ortho and para positions the most electron-deficient, so meta attack is least disfavoured.
$-OCH_3$, $-NHCOCH_3$ and $-Cl$ all have a lone pair on the attached atom, so they are o/p directors.
solution.why_not_others: $-OCH_3$ and $-NHCOCH_3$ are activating o/p directors. $-Cl$ is deactivating but still o/p directing because of its +R effect.
solution.common_trap: Treating $-Cl$ as meta directing because it is deactivating. Halogens are deactivating but o/p directing.
solution.time_saving_tip: Check the atom attached to the ring. A lone pair means o/p; a pi bond to O or N, or a positive charge, means meta.

questions.question: The correct order of reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is:
options: phenol > toluene > benzene > chlorobenzene > nitrobenzene
toluene > phenol > benzene > chlorobenzene > nitrobenzene
phenol > toluene > chlorobenzene > benzene > nitrobenzene
phenol > benzene > toluene > nitrobenzene > chlorobenzene

solution.key_concept: Activating groups increase the rate of substitution, halogens deactivate mildly and the nitro group deactivates strongly.
steps: $-OH$ is strongly activating through its +R effect, so phenol is the most reactive.
$-CH_3$ activates weakly by +I and hyperconjugation, so toluene is more reactive than benzene.
$-Cl$ is deactivating because its -I effect dominates, so chlorobenzene is less reactive than benzene.
$-NO_2$ is strongly deactivating by -R/-I, so nitrobenzene is the least reactive.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): phenol > toluene > benzene > chlorobenzene > nitrobenzene
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) ranks methyl above hydroxyl, but $-OH$ activates more strongly. Option (3) treats Cl as activating. Option (4) places toluene below benzene and nitrobenzene above chlorobenzene.
solution.common_trap: Assuming chlorobenzene is more reactive than benzene because Cl is an o/p director.

questions.question: Nitration of aniline with a mixture of concentrated $HNO_3$ and $H_2SO_4$ gives a substantial amount of the meta-nitro product. The best explanation is that:
options: the $-NH_2$ group is inherently meta directing
in the strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, and $-NH_3^+$ is meta directing
the $-NH_2$ group is deactivating because of the -I effect of nitrogen
steric hindrance completely blocks both the ortho and the para positions

solution.key_concept: A positively charged group on the atom attached to the ring is a meta-directing deactivating group.
steps: Free $-NH_2$ has a lone pair on N, so it is an activating o/p director.
In strongly acidic nitrating mixture, aniline is protonated to $C_6H_5NH_3^+$.
$-NH_3^+$ carries a positive charge and no lone pair, so it withdraws electrons and directs to meta.
Therefore a substantial amount of meta product forms.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): in the strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, and $-NH_3^+$ is meta directing
solution.why_not_others: Free $-NH_2$ is an activating o/p director. Its +R effect makes it activating, not deactivating. Steric hindrance cannot block the para position.
solution.common_trap: Concluding that $-NH_2$ itself is meta directing because a meta product is obtained.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution faster than benzene.
statements.R: The chlorine atom in chlorobenzene directs an incoming electrophile to the ortho and para positions through its +R effect.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Halogens are deactivating because their -I effect dominates, but they are o/p directing because of their +R effect.
steps: The strong -I effect of Cl lowers the overall electron density of the ring.
So chlorobenzene is less reactive than benzene, and A is false.
The +R effect of Cl still raises electron density at the ortho and para positions relative to meta, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so any option that calls A true is wrong. The direction of attack (R) does not determine the overall rate.
solution.common_trap: Treating halogens as activating because they are o/p directing.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In nitrobenzene, the meta positions are the most electron-deficient positions of the ring, and this is why nitration of nitrobenzene gives m-dinitrobenzene.
statements.II: The $-NHCOCH_3$ group is a meta-directing group because the nitrogen attached to the ring is bonded to a $C=O$ group.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Meta directors make the ortho and para positions most electron-deficient, so meta attack is only the least disfavoured. A lone pair on the atom attached to the ring makes a group an o/p director.
steps: $-NO_2$ withdraws electrons by -R/-I, so the ortho and para positions become the most electron-deficient.
Meta attack is therefore the least disfavoured, not favoured because meta is the most electron-deficient. Statement I is incorrect.
In $-NHCOCH_3$, the ring is attached to N, which carries a lone pair.
So $-NHCOCH_3$ is an activating o/p director, and Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement I gives the right product (m-dinitrobenzene) but the wrong reason. Statement II wrongly judges the group by the carbonyl, which is not attached to the ring.
solution.common_trap: Accepting Statement I because its product is correct, and labelling $-NHCOCH_3$ meta directing because it contains $C=O$.
solution.time_saving_tip: Look only at the atom bonded directly to the ring when deciding the directing effect.
